questions.prompt: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 10 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A ball is thrown horizontally at 25 m s⁻¹ from a height of 78.4 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How far from the foot of the height does it land? (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 15 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 10 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 10 m s⁻¹ at 45° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the time of flight. (answer in s, number only.)
A body moving at 5 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻² for 5 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 2 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 10 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 10 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)

A 5 kg cart moving at 2 m s⁻¹ collides head-on with a 5 kg cart moving in the opposite direction at 2 m s⁻¹. What is the total momentum before the collision? (take the first cart’s direction as positive) (answer in kg m s⁻¹, number only.)
questions.explanation: p = m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = 5(2) + 5(−2) = 0 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: The path followed by a projectile is called its ______.
questions.explanation: The path followed by a projectile is called its trajectory. Trajectory = the path of the projectile.

questions.prompt: The time taken by a ball to rise to its highest point is ______ the time taken to fall back to the launch level.
questions.explanation: The time taken by a ball to rise to its highest point is equal to the time taken to fall back to the launch level. Symmetric motion: t_up = v_i/g = t_down.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 15 m s⁻¹ at 60° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the time of flight. (answer in s, number only.)
The path of a projectile in the absence of air resistance is a ______.
questions.explanation: The path of a projectile in the absence of air resistance is a parabola. Uniform horizontal motion plus uniformly accelerated vertical motion gives a parabola.

questions.prompt: A car moving at 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 3 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
For a body starting from rest, v_i = ______ in the equations of motion.
questions.explanation: For a body starting from rest, v_i = 0 in the equations of motion. Starting from rest means the initial velocity is zero.

questions.prompt: For a given launch speed, the range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is ______.
questions.explanation: For a given launch speed, the range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is 45°. sin2θ = 1 when 2θ = 90°.

questions.prompt: The equations of motion are valid only when the acceleration is ______.
questions.explanation: The equations of motion are valid only when the acceleration is constant. They were derived for uniform (constant) acceleration along a straight line.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 50 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
A 1 kg body moving at 12 m s⁻¹ makes an angle of 30° with the x-axis. What is the x-component of its momentum? (answer in kg m s⁻¹, number only.)
questions.explanation: p_x = mv cosθ = 1 × 12 × cos30° = 10.4 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A 1 kg body moving at 6 m s⁻¹ hits a 9 kg body at rest and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost? (answer in J, number only.)
Because of air resistance, the horizontal component of a projectile’s velocity ______.
questions.explanation: Because of air resistance, the horizontal component of a projectile’s velocity decreases. The drag has a horizontal part opposite to the motion.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 40 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 10 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 8 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A 4 kg trolley moving at 10 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 1 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the second trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
Because of air resistance, the maximum height of a projectile is ______.
questions.explanation: Because of air resistance, the maximum height of a projectile is reduced. The upward velocity is lost faster.

questions.prompt: A body moving at 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻² for 10 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body thrown into the air that then moves only under gravity is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A body thrown into the air that then moves only under gravity is called a projectile. A projectile moves under gravity alone (air resistance neglected).

questions.prompt: The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of an isolated system ______.
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant. Δp = 0 for an isolated system.

questions.prompt: If a moving body slows down, the sign of its acceleration is ______ the sign of its velocity.
questions.explanation: If a moving body slows down, the sign of its acceleration is opposite to the sign of its velocity. Retardation is acceleration opposite to the velocity, so it is negative when v is positive.

questions.prompt: A body moving at 5 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 3 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 8 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 6 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 20 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 5 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 10 m s⁻¹ at 37° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the time of flight. (answer in s, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 30 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
A body’s velocity changes uniformly from 0 m s⁻¹ to 24 m s⁻¹ in 8 s. What is its acceleration? (answer in m s⁻², number only.)
The kinetic energy of a projectile is least at the ______.
questions.explanation: The kinetic energy of a projectile is least at the highest point. The speed is least there.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally at 30 m s⁻¹ from a height of 4.9 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) With what speed does it hit the ground? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 15 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 8 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 10 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 5 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 20 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻² for 8 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 5 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 10 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
The slope of a distance–time graph gives the ______.
questions.explanation: The slope of a distance–time graph gives the velocity. Slope = ΔS/Δt = v.

questions.prompt: A car moving at 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 5 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m s⁻¹ from a height of 4.9 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How far from the foot of the height does it land? (answer in m, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 20 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 6 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 10 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 3 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m s⁻¹ from a height of 78.4 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) With what speed does it hit the ground? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
The area under a velocity–time graph gives the ______ (displacement).
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity–time graph gives the distance (displacement). Area = v × t summed over the motion = distance travelled.

questions.prompt: A body moving at 15 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 3 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A car moving at 6 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 4 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A car moving at 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 8 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 10 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A ball is thrown horizontally at 8 m s⁻¹ from a height of 44.1 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) With what speed does it hit the ground? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
The time of flight of a projectile depends on ______ motion only.
questions.explanation: The time of flight of a projectile depends on vertical motion only. T is fixed by the vertical component and g.

questions.prompt: In a perfectly inelastic collision the kinetic energy loss is ______.
questions.explanation: In a perfectly inelastic collision the kinetic energy loss is maximum. The bodies move with a common velocity.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 30 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
For two complementary launch angles with the same speed, the one with the larger angle has the ______ maximum height.
questions.explanation: For two complementary launch angles with the same speed, the one with the larger angle has the larger maximum height. H ∝ sin²θ.

questions.prompt: A collision in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved is called an ______ collision.
questions.explanation: A collision in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved is called an elastic collision. Both are conserved only in elastic collisions.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally at 25 m s⁻¹ from a height of 19.6 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) With what speed does it hit the ground? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 50 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the time of flight. (answer in s, number only.)
A ball is thrown horizontally at 15 m s⁻¹ from a height of 19.6 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How far from the foot of the height does it land? (answer in m, number only.)
A 5 kg trolley moving at 18 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 1 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the second trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
The horizontal acceleration of a projectile (air resistance neglected) is ______.
questions.explanation: The horizontal acceleration of a projectile (air resistance neglected) is zero. a_x = 0.

questions.prompt: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 5 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 10 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 3 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A person on a skateboard throws a heavy ball forward. The skateboard moves ______.
questions.explanation: A person on a skateboard throws a heavy ball forward. The skateboard moves backward. Backward momentum balances the ball’s forward momentum.

questions.prompt: The branch of mechanics that studies the causes of motion, that is, the forces, is called ______.
questions.explanation: The branch of mechanics that studies the causes of motion, that is, the forces, is called dynamics. Dynamics deals with forces and the motion they produce.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 40 m s⁻¹ at 45° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the time of flight. (answer in s, number only.)
Momentum is a ______ quantity.
questions.explanation: Momentum is a vector quantity. Its direction is the direction of the velocity.

questions.prompt: The equation of motion that does not contain the distance S is the ______ equation.
questions.explanation: The equation of motion that does not contain the distance S is the first equation. v_f = v_i + at has v_i, v_f, a and t only.

questions.prompt: Acceleration is the rate of change of ______.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. a = (v_f − v_i)/t: acceleration measures how quickly velocity changes.

questions.prompt: The area under an acceleration–time graph gives the change in ______.
questions.explanation: The area under an acceleration–time graph gives the change in velocity. Area = a × t = Δv.

questions.prompt: When a ball bounces back from a wall with the same speed, the ball’s momentum changes by ______ in magnitude.
questions.explanation: When a ball bounces back from a wall with the same speed, the ball’s momentum changes by 2mu in magnitude. From +mu to −mu: change = −2mu.

questions.prompt: For a horizontal launch, the time of flight depends only on the ______ of the launch point.
questions.explanation: For a horizontal launch, the time of flight depends only on the height of the launch point. t = √(2h/g) does not contain v_i.

questions.prompt: For a body that comes to rest, v_f = ______ in the equations of motion.
questions.explanation: For a body that comes to rest, v_f = 0 in the equations of motion. Coming to rest means the final velocity is zero.

questions.prompt: Horizontal and vertical motions of a projectile are ______ motions.
questions.explanation: Horizontal and vertical motions of a projectile are independent motions. Gravity acts only downward, so it does not affect the horizontal motion.

A body moving at 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻² for 10 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)

A projectile is launched at 30 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻² for 5 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
Two bodies exert forces on each other during a collision. These forces are equal in magnitude and ______ in direction.
questions.explanation: Two bodies exert forces on each other during a collision. These forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. Newton’s third law, so the total momentum change is zero.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg body moving at 6 m s⁻¹ hits a 1 kg body at rest and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost? (answer in J, number only.)
Two identical bodies collide elastically; one is initially at rest. If it is not a head-on collision, the angle between their paths after the collision is ______.
questions.explanation: Two identical bodies collide elastically; one is initially at rest. If it is not a head-on collision, the angle between their paths after the collision is 90°. Equal masses and elastic: v₁′ · v₂′ = 0.

questions.prompt: The time taken by a projectile to go up to the highest point is ______ the time taken to come down to the same level.
questions.explanation: The time taken by a projectile to go up to the highest point is equal to the time taken to come down to the same level. The path is symmetric about the top.

questions.prompt: At the highest point of a ball thrown vertically upward, the velocity is ______ but the acceleration is g downward.
questions.explanation: At the highest point of a ball thrown vertically upward, the velocity is zero but the acceleration is g downward. v = 0 for an instant; a = g throughout the motion.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg trolley moving at 4 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 1 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the first trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)

A ball is thrown horizontally at 30 m s⁻¹ from a height of 19.6 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How far from the foot of the height does it land? (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 8 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 8 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 4 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 5 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 5 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A car moving at 10 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 6 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A 3 kg trolley moving at 12 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 3 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the second trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
Air resistance ______ the energy and the velocity of a projectile.
questions.explanation: Air resistance decreases the energy and the velocity of a projectile. It does negative work on the body.

questions.prompt: A car moving at 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 4 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 37° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 3 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 15 m s⁻¹ at 45° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 15 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 6 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A car moving at 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 2 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A car moving at 10 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 2 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
In an elastic collision the total ______ is conserved along with momentum.
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision the total kinetic energy is conserved along with momentum. K before = K after.

questions.prompt: A 1 kg trolley moving at 8 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 3 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the first trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A car moving at 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 5 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A car moving at 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 5 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 40 m s⁻¹ at 45° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 5 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m s⁻² for 3 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
In the equation m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = m₁v₁′ + m₂v₂′, the primed velocities are those ______ the collision.
questions.explanation: In the equation m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = m₁v₁′ + m₂v₂′, the primed velocities are those after the collision. Primes denote the final velocities.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 40 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
Two bodies of different mass have the same momentum. The one with the smaller mass has the ______ kinetic energy.
questions.explanation: Two bodies of different mass have the same momentum. The one with the smaller mass has the greater kinetic energy. K = p²/2m is larger for smaller m.

questions.prompt: If the mass of a moving body is doubled at the same speed, its momentum becomes ______.
questions.explanation: If the mass of a moving body is doubled at the same speed, its momentum becomes doubled. p ∝ m.

questions.prompt: A car moving at 12 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 3 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
The range of a projectile is proportional to the square of the ______.
questions.explanation: The range of a projectile is proportional to the square of the launch speed. R ∝ v_i² for a fixed angle.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 15 m s⁻¹ at 60° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
For two complementary launch angles with the same speed, the one with the larger angle has the ______ time of flight.
questions.explanation: For two complementary launch angles with the same speed, the one with the larger angle has the longer time of flight. T ∝ sinθ.

questions.prompt: When a body at rest explodes into two fragments, the lighter fragment moves with the ______ speed.
questions.explanation: When a body at rest explodes into two fragments, the lighter fragment moves with the greater speed. m₁v₁ = m₂v₂ in magnitude.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 25 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
A body moving at 12 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 4 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A body moving at 20 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 8 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 15 m s⁻¹ at 37° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height. (answer in m, number only.)
In an elastic collision, the relative speed of approach is ______ the relative speed of separation.
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision, the relative speed of approach is equal to the relative speed of separation. u₁ − u₂ = v₂ − v₁.

questions.prompt: A rocket moves forward because the expelled gases carry ______ momentum.
questions.explanation: A rocket moves forward because the expelled gases carry backward momentum. Conservation of momentum: the rocket gains forward momentum.

questions.prompt: Near the Earth’s surface, with air resistance neglected, all freely falling bodies have the same acceleration of about ______ m s⁻².
questions.explanation: Near the Earth’s surface, with air resistance neglected, all freely falling bodies have the same acceleration of about 9.8 m s⁻². g = 9.8 m s⁻² (the book quotes 9.81).

questions.prompt: A body moving at 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻² for 4 s. What is its final velocity? (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
The branch of mechanics that studies motion without considering its causes is called ______.
questions.explanation: The branch of mechanics that studies motion without considering its causes is called kinematics. Kinematics describes motion (displacement, velocity, acceleration) without asking what causes it.

questions.prompt: If a moving body hits a body at rest and both then move along the x-axis, the total y-momentum is ______.
questions.explanation: If a moving body hits a body at rest and both then move along the x-axis, the total y-momentum is zero. It was zero before the collision.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m s⁻¹ from a height of 19.6 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How far from the foot of the height does it land? (answer in m, number only.)
A body’s velocity changes uniformly from 0 m s⁻¹ to 16 m s⁻¹ in 2 s. What is its acceleration? (answer in m s⁻², number only.)
A 2 kg trolley moving at 10 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 3 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the first trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
The same three equations of motion are used for free fall by replacing a with ______.
questions.explanation: The same three equations of motion are used for free fall by replacing a with g. a = g = 9.8 m s⁻².

questions.prompt: Both momentum and ______ are conserved in an elastic collision, but only momentum is conserved in an inelastic one.
questions.explanation: Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved in an elastic collision, but only momentum is conserved in an inelastic one. This is the key difference.

questions.prompt: The speed of a projectile is smallest at the ______ of its path.
questions.explanation: The speed of a projectile is smallest at the highest point of its path. There v_y = 0, so the speed is only v_i cosθ.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally at 30 m s⁻¹ from a height of 78.4 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) At what angle below the horizontal does it strike the ground? (answer in °, number only.)
A karate player breaks a pile of tiles because the large momentum of his hand is reduced to zero in a very ______ time.
questions.explanation: A karate player breaks a pile of tiles because the large momentum of his hand is reduced to zero in a very short time. A short time gives a large force.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 10 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
Two bodies of different mass have the same momentum. The one with the smaller mass has the ______ speed.
questions.explanation: Two bodies of different mass have the same momentum. The one with the smaller mass has the greater speed. v = p/m.

questions.prompt: Because of air resistance, the range of a projectile is ______.
questions.explanation: Because of air resistance, the range of a projectile is reduced. A slower projectile covers less horizontal distance.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally from a table and another ball is dropped from the same height at the same instant. The two balls hit the ground at the ______.
questions.explanation: A ball is thrown horizontally from a table and another ball is dropped from the same height at the same instant. The two balls hit the ground at the same time. Vertical motion is identical: both start with v_y = 0 and fall with a = g.

questions.prompt: On a v–t graph of a body starting from rest and accelerating uniformly, the distance is the area of a ______.
questions.explanation: On a v–t graph of a body starting from rest and accelerating uniformly, the distance is the area of a triangle. Area = ½ t v_f = ½at².

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 30 m s⁻¹ at 37° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
A 2 kg body moving at 6 m s⁻¹ hits a 3 kg body at rest and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost? (answer in J, number only.)
A 1 kg trolley moving at 4 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 3 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the first trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A 3 kg trolley moving at 15 m s⁻¹ collides elastically head-on with a 2 kg trolley at rest. Find the velocity of the second trolley after the collision. (answer in m s⁻¹, number only.)
A car moving at 12 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 2 s. How far does it travel in this time? (answer in m, number only.)
A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 60° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the range. (answer in m, number only.)
A heavy body hits a very light body at rest elastically. The light body moves off at about ______ the speed of the heavy body.
questions.explanation: A heavy body hits a very light body at rest elastically. The light body moves off at about twice the speed of the heavy body. v₂ = 2m₁u₁/(m₁ + m₂) ≈ 2u₁.

questions.prompt: A body’s velocity changes uniformly from 10 m s⁻¹ to 50 m s⁻¹ in 8 s. What is its acceleration? (answer in m s⁻², number only.)
